newsitem.title: NEPAL: Nepali finance minister Mahat reappointed.
newsitem.headline: Nepali finance minister Mahat reappointed.

text.p: Nepali Prime Minister Sher Bahadur Deuba on Thursday reappointed Ram Sharan Mahat as the Himalayan kingdom's finance minister three months after he was forced by the opposition to resign, Radio Nepal said.

The appointment of the liberal economist raises to 48 the total members of the cabinet headed by Deuba, who has been criticised for the large size of the government in the tiny kingdom, among the world's 10 poorest countries.

Mahat resigned as finance minister in July after opposition communists stalled proceedings in the House of Representatives, the lower house of Parliament, demanding his dismissal over an account at New York-based Chemical Bank.
Deuba kept the portfolio of the finance ministry to himself in the interim three months.
The kingdom's laws do not allow Nepali nationals to maintain foreign bank accounts without the approval of the central bank.
The communists said the minister had flouted the foreign exchange regulations.
Mahat said the account was opened when he worked for the United Nations Development Programme (UNDP). But he bowed out, saying his action would set moral precedence among politicians.
Before entering Nepali politics five years ago, Mahat served with the UNDP in New York.
A government department probing irregularities in foreign exchange transactions recently cleared Mahat.
Mahat, 45, was the architect of the liberal economic policy adopted in 1992 to attract foreign investment to the kingdom.
He belongs to Deuba's Nepali Congress party, which is leading a three party centre-right coalition government that replaced a communist administration last year.

Deuba has justified the relatively large size of the cabinet as a product of the hung parliament that emerged from mid-term elections in 1994 and spurred claims for cabinet positions from the three parties in the ruling coalition.
